title: Dogfood and the pilot
bridge: Dogfooding Nova is like trying a new deploy script on your own side project before the main app. Except: the side project here is the repo that builds Nova itself. So a repo policy must stop Nova from editing the hooks, judges and checks that hold it.
intro: Before any fcp ticket, Nova runs on 5 to 8 small tickets in its own repo, RhinoHealth/ai-agents. Then the guilds pick the first fcp tickets, and a one-page how-to tells people how to hand one over. Every week from W9 to W12, Sean and one reviewer per guild read every Nova PR.

picture.caption: From our own repo to fcp, with a weekly read of every PR.

steps.text: assigns 5 to 8 small ai-agents tickets to Nova

each run's transcript and receipt are read; problems become tickets

p: The first Nova PRs should not land in fcp. Our own repo, RhinoHealth/ai-agents, is the safest place to find rough edges. The reviewers built Nova, and nothing customer-facing changes. Using your own tool first is called dogfooding.
Pick 5 to 8 RH tickets with the component ai-agents: docs, tests, Slack message copy, small orchestrator bugs. Nothing that touches the walls. The dogfood runs in W8 and W9.

Each repo Nova works in has a repo policy: a YAML file in ai-agents/config/repos/. It names the verify command, the paths Nova may never edit, the reviewers and the VM size. The broker and the harness read it.

sections.h: The dogfood policy: Nova cannot edit what holds it
p: In ai-agents, the code that judges and walls Nova sits next to the code Nova may fix. So the protected paths list is long. It covers the hooks, the judges, the required checks, the broker, the gateway, the evals and the settings.
The same paths sit in ai-agents's block of settings/protected-paths.yaml, which the harness hooks and the broker enforce. ai-agents has no UI, so a lite VM is enough and the QA agent is not needed.
sections.because: Agents never change the checks they are judged by, and in this repo those checks are one folder away.

code.text:
# ai-agents/config/repos/ai-agents.yaml: Nova's policy for dogfooding on its own repo. Format per G3's broker allow-list.
repo: RhinoHealth/ai-agents
branch_prefix: nova/
verify: "npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build"   # what ai-agents CI runs (G3), the same commands people use; confirm
protected_paths:                # a wall: Nova never edits what enforces the walls or judges it (ai-agents's block in settings/protected-paths.yaml)
  - ".github/workflows/**"
  - "harness/src/hooks.ts"        # the walls (G3-21)
  - "harness/src/hooks/**"
  - "harness/src/checks/**"       # false-heal and proof checks (G5)
  - "harness/src/judges/**"
  - "harness/prompts/pr-judge.md"
  - "checks/**"                 # the required checks: independent approval, locked checks, weakened tests
  - "broker/**"
  - "gateway/**"
  - "evals/**"
  - "config/**"
  - "settings/**"                # managed settings, spend limits, protected paths
  - "packer/**"
ask_first_paths: []             # fcp uses this for the pilot scope (migrations, auth, gRPC); nothing here
reviewers:
  team: ai-agents-maintainers   # GitHub team to create; exactly 1 approval, never the requester
sandbox: lite                   # no UI and no FCP Lab needed
jira:
  project: RH
  component: ai-agents

p: Hand each ticket over the normal way: assign it to Nova. Pieces that are not ready yet, like the Byte loop or the ready gate, are done by hand and noted.
After each run, read the transcript and the receipt. File each problem as a ticket. Put each "this should be a check or a skill line" in the harness-suggestions list.
Approval follows the same rule as fcp: one person who is not the requester. Dogfood is not an exception.

callout.text: Exactly one approval, never the requester, in ai-agents too. Sean assigns a dogfood ticket, so another maintainer approves its PR.

p: With the FE and BE guild leads, gather 5 to 10 fcp tickets in a Jira filter. Good ones: small FE bugs, missing tests, small BE fixes. Not migrations, auth, infra or the cloud-client gRPC contract.

fcp's policy uses ask_first_paths for that scope. These are a choice people made while we learn, not a wall. When an edit lands there, Nova stops and asks the requester. Workflow files stay protected, which is a wall.
The verify commands are G7's npm run verify and poe verify. Until they land, Nova uses the checking guide's commands (lesson g4-3).
sections.because: Starting narrow keeps the first PRs small to review and proves the loop works before the scope grows.

code.text:
# ai-agents/config/repos/fcp.yaml (a sketch built from G4-28's steps, in the dogfood file's format)
repo: RhinoHealth/fcp
branch_prefix: nova/
verify:                                     # G7's commands; until they land, the checking guide's commands
  frontend: "npm run verify"
  backend: "poe verify"
protected_paths:                            # a wall: Nova never edits these
  - ".github/workflows/**"
ask_first_paths:                            # the pilot scope: a choice by people, Nova stops and asks
  - "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/migrations/**"
  - "client/rhinoOnPrem/*/migrations/**"
  - "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoDjango/login/**"
  - "frontend/src/app/(auth)/**"
  - "frontend/src/app/api/auth/**"
  - "common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/**"
reviewers:                                  # exactly 1 approval, never the requester
  by_path:
    "frontend/**": frontend-guild
    "cloud/**": backend-guild
    "client/**": backend-guild
jira:
  project: RH

sections.h: One page: how to hand a ticket to Nova
p: People need one short page, not a manual. It lives in RhinoHealth/rnd-kb (decision 6, the brain's location, is still to confirm with Nave and Shai). Post it in #engineering.
Then do a 20-minute walk-through at a guild meeting: assign a ticket live, approve its plan, open the PR.
sections.because: A hand-off that people can do from memory is what makes the pilot real, not the code behind it.

code.text:
---
# rnd-kb page frontmatter (owner, review date, confidence, sources): format per G6, not final
owner: sean
review_by: 2027-01-15
confidence: medium
sources: [G4 plan, RhinoHealth/ai-agents README]
---
# How to hand a ticket to Nova

**Good first tickets:** a small FE bug, missing tests, a small BE fix. Not migrations, auth, infra or the gRPC contract.

1. **Assign the Jira ticket to "Nova".** You become the requester and stay the owner. (Or `/nova RH-1234` in Slack.)
2. **Answer its questions.** For bigger tickets Nova asks first, in the ticket and in Slack. Reply with `@Nova`.
3. **Approve the plan.** It starts with what "done" means and 3–5 checks. Approve, Change or Stop in Slack.
4. **Wait for a ready PR.** Nova keeps it in draft until CI is green and Byte's important findings are handled.
   The ticket comes back to you then.
5. **Someone else approves.** One approval from a person who is not you; you can't approve your own Nova PR.

**To stop:** unassign Nova, or comment `@Nova stop`. The branch and notes are kept.
**Something odd?** Say so in the ticket's Slack thread. Every week we read all Nova PRs together.

The pilot scope in one line.
Step 1: assignment is the hand-off (lesson g4-1). The person who assigns is the requester.
Step 2: the grill (lesson g4-2). Reply with @Nova.
Step 3: done and 3 to 5 checks, then Approve, Change or Stop.
Step 4: the draft and the ready gate (lesson g4-6). The ticket comes back to you then.
Step 5: one approval, never the requester.
Unassign Nova or comment @Nova stop. The branch and notes are kept.

p: Every week from W9 to W12, Sean and one reviewer from each guild read every Nova PR and its run. That takes about 30 minutes a week from each guild reviewer.

nova_weekly.py builds the table before the meeting. It lists the week's Nova PRs with their state, requester and approvers, and flags any PR its requester approved. Run it with uv run --project evals python evals/reports/nova_weekly.py <since>.
Cost, minutes, receipt counts and scope-judge vetoes come from the run records, joined by Jira key.
sections.because: The flag column checks the most important wall by hand every week, on top of the G0 check.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/reports/nova_weekly.py: the table for the weekly Nova PR review. Python, in the evals uv project.
import json
import subprocess
import sys


def gh(*args: str) -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads(subprocess.run(["gh", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)


since = sys.argv[1]  # e.g. 2026-11-23
prs = gh("pr", "list", "--repo", "RhinoHealth/fcp", "--author", "app/rhino-ai-agents", "--state", "all",
         "--search", f"created:>={since}", "--json", "number,title,state,body,latestReviews")
print("| PR | Title | State | Requester | Approver | Requester approved? |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
for pr in prs:
    lines = pr["body"].splitlines()
    requester = next((ln.split("@", 1)[1].strip() for ln in lines if ln.startswith("Requested-by: @")), "?")
    approvers = [r["author"]["login"] for r in pr["latestReviews"] if r["state"] == "APPROVED"]
    flag = "YES, look into it" if requester in approvers else "no"
    print(f"| #{pr['number']} | {pr['title'][:60]} | {pr['state']} | {requester} | {', '.join(approvers) or '-'} | {flag} |")
# Cost, minutes, receipt counts and scope-judge vetoes come from the run records (S3, gateway tags; G0, G1), joined by Jira key.

notes.text: Python, next to the bench code, so reports live in one place.
The same small gh helper as mine.py: run gh, parse JSON.
The first day of the week, for example 2026-11-23.
Only PRs authored by Nova's GitHub App, in any state.
Each reviewer's latest review, enough to see who approved.
Read the login from the Requested-by line, or ? if it is missing.
Everyone whose latest review is APPROVED.
The requester is among the approvers: the wall failed somewhere. Look into it.
The rest of the meeting's numbers come from the run records.

p: The pilot aims for 10 merged tickets by mid-December and at least half of Nova's PRs merged. The number of PRs approved by their own requester must stay 0.
Track these week by week, plus PRs with full proof: QA results, receipt and trace link. For each closed PR, write one line on why. For the 3 longest runs, ask one question: was the time well spent?

Harness suggestions become tickets: a new check, a new bench task, or a skill line. A skill line ships only if it raises TICKET-BENCH pass@1 (lesson g4-7). Notes go to rnd-kb as summaries, with no customer data.

callout.text: Time and cost in the weekly table are for learning. A long run is a question for the meeting, never a reason to add a limit.

lab.title: Check the policies and the weekly table (reading lab)

worked.do: Nova's dogfood ticket asks for a better Slack message in slack-app/src/messages.ts. Is the path protected?
worked.see: No. slack-app/ is not in protected_paths, so Nova may edit it.

worked.do: The same run wants to change harness/src/judges/scope.ts to make the scope judge less strict. What happens?
worked.see: Denied: harness/src/judges/** is protected. The hook refuses the edit and the broker refuses the push.

worked.do: In fcp, an edit lands in client/rhinoOnPrem/rhinoAgent/migrations/0042_x.py. Wall or choice?
worked.see: A choice: the path matches client/rhinoOnPrem/*/migrations/**, an ask-first path. Nova stops and asks the requester.

worked.do: In nova_weekly.py, a PR body ends with Requested-by: @dana. latestReviews has dana APPROVED and omer APPROVED. What is the flag?
worked.see: YES, look into it. dana is the requester and is among the approvers.

worked.do: A PR body has no Requested-by line. What does the table show?
worked.see: Requester ? and flag no. The G0 check fails such a PR closed, so it should never merge; note it in the meeting.

lab.faded: Write the how-to page's "Something odd?" line for Slack-only users. Add one more line on stopping a run from Slack. The exact wording is left to you; keep each line under 20 words.
lab.alone: Write ai-agents/config/repos/rnd-kb.yaml for a future Nova on the brain repo, in the dogfood format. Decide its protected paths (hint: DATA-SCOPE.md, OWNERS.yml, templates and .github), the reviewers and the VM size, with one comment per choice.
lab.done: For any path you can say: edit, ask first, or refused. You can also read every column of the weekly table.

quiz.q: Why does Nova run on ai-agents tickets before fcp tickets?

options.text: ai-agents has no walls, so Nova can move faster
options.why: ai-agents has the longest protected-paths list of all, because Nova's own walls live there.

options.text: Its reviewers built Nova and nothing customer-facing changes, so rough edges are cheap to find
options.why: That is the reason in G4-22: the safest place to learn.

options.text: PRs in ai-agents need no approval
options.why: Same rule as fcp: one person who is not the requester.

quiz.q: In fcp, Nova's edit lands in frontend/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx. What happens?

options.text: Nova stops and asks the requester: it is an ask-first path
options.why: Auth is in the pilot scope that people chose to keep out while we learn.

options.text: The hook refuses it forever: it is a protected path
options.why: In fcp only .github/workflows/** is protected. Auth is ask-first.

options.text: Nothing; Nova may edit any frontend file
options.why: The policy lists frontend/src/app/(auth)/** under ask_first_paths.

quiz.q: The weekly table shows YES in "Requester approved?". What does that mean?

options.text: Normal: the requester knows the ticket best
options.why: The requester never approves their own agent's PR. The target is 0.

options.text: A wall failed somewhere; look into how the PR was approved
options.why: The count of requester-approved PRs must stay 0, so every YES is investigated.

options.text: Fine, as long as a second person also approved
options.why: The rule is about who counts: the requester's approval never counts, whoever else approved.
